positions.stance: Committed to giving elementary and secondary schools the resources they need and to making college more affordable and accessible.
Believes America needs to lead the world in developing new, clean and sustainable power sources, and advocates investment in energy efficiency and renewable energy.
Supports bringing U.S. troops home from the Middle East "in a responsible manner" and requiring congressional authorization before military force is used in Syria.
Fighting to give Santa Clara families and businesses tools to grow, and to drive economic growth that puts Americans to work in good jobs.
Supported the Affordable Care Act and opposes any "heedless dismantling" of health policies that cover families and individuals.

H0CA32101.name: Judy Chu
H0CA32101.bio: Former community college professor and school board member; member of the House Ways and Means Committee.

positions.stance: Working to increase protections for public lands and waters, including recreation opportunities and federal protections in the San Gabriel Mountains.
Says sweeping tariffs are taxes paid by American importers that raise prices for families and small businesses already facing high housing and living costs.
Supports fully funding education programs and guaranteeing equal opportunity for all students "from pre-K through college and beyond."
Committed to protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act and protecting Medicare; says no one should be denied treatment for preexisting conditions.
Calls the immigration system "broken, outdated" and supports reform that is humane, efficient and accessible, opposing a mass-deportation agenda.
Prioritizes legislation that will "create a fairer economy, strengthen our nation's democracy and improve equity for all Americans."

H4CA33119.name: Ted Lieu
H4CA33119.bio: U.S. Representative and immigrant from Taiwan.

positions.stance: "I am fully committed to ensuring and protecting the civil rights of all Americans"; stands against racial, cultural or religious intolerance.
Says solving climate change requires America to do what California has done, including investing in green energy, strong renewable standards and slashing carbon pollution.

H6CA36208.name: Houston Brignano
H6CA36208.bio: Marine veteran who served in Iraq.

positions.stance: Promises "radical transparency to every dollar spent," publishing every meeting, donor and vote explanation online and taking no corporate PAC money.
Would create innovation zones for technology, manufacturing and energy jobs and streamline regulations he says drive up California's costs.
Supports portable health savings accounts, cross-state insurance competition and price transparency before patients are billed.

H2CA43245.name: Mark Takano
H2CA43245.bio: Former teacher of more than 20 years and senior member of the House Education and Workforce Committee.

positions.stance: Says future prosperity requires strong investment in public education and workforce training, and supports updating work standards "passed down from a different era."
Calls poor air quality from warehouse-driven traffic and emissions a major health threat in the Inland Empire and has presented potential policy solutions.
Committed to ensuring the jobs at March Air Reserve Base, the largest employer in his district, are protected.
Says all Americans deserve quality, affordable health care and that Congress needs to pass legislation because the current system is not working for all.
Says Congress must restore funding for housing assistance and counseling; supports reforms helping homeowners refinance and making foreclosure more consumer friendly.

H2CA37023.name: Ken Calvert
H2CA37023.bio: U.S. Representative and Chairman of the House Defense Appropriations Subcommittee.

positions.stance: Says government must address farmers' challenges such as pests, water shortages, regulatory burdens and unfair trade barriers, expand markets, and provide emergency assistance when needed.
Dedicated to restoring military readiness and modernizing capabilities to curb adversaries such as Russia and China and hold Iran and North Korea accountable.
Supports reevaluating the federal role in education, balancing standards and accountability with the rights of students, families and teachers while preserving local K-12 control.
Supports increasing domestic energy production in the short term and major long-term investment in energy-efficient and renewable technologies.
Working on patient-centered reforms to increase access and lower costs while protecting people with pre-existing conditions and dependent coverage to age 26.

H2CA38260.name: Mitch Clemmons
H2CA38260.bio: Local plumbing contractor and small business owner.

positions.stance: Calls election integrity "the foundation of everything" and pledges to fight to secure elections so the people's voice is heard.
Supports restoring law and order by treating homelessness humanely with accountability, cracking down on small crimes early, and ending taxpayer-funded fraud through NGOs.
Wants schools to teach "skills and values — never ideology" and says parents should have the final say in raising their children.

H6CA46116.name: Lou Correa
H6CA46116.bio: U.S. Representative and member of the House Committee on Homeland Security.

positions.stance: Promotes educational policies that ensure all students reach their full potential and has worked on legislation to help more people go to college.
Working to ensure the EPA adheres to standards that protect clean air and water, and supports energy independence without harming the environment.
Calls affordable, quality health care a top priority; opposed repealing the Affordable Care Act and deep cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.
Supports DREAMers and continues to advocate for comprehensive immigration reform.
Says the path to the middle class starts with a good job; supports legislation to drive innovation and help local businesses and entrepreneurs.

H6CA51140.name: Ricardo Cabrera
H6CA51140.bio: San Diego small business owner and cybersecurity professional.

positions.stance: Supports congressional term limits, saying Washington needs citizen legislators, not career politicians.
Wants to fight for affordability and policies that let working families live, work and build a future in California.
Supports fiscal responsibility, public safety and a government focused on results instead of bureaucracy.
"I will always fight to support family farms, protect private property rights," and help Texans continue living off the land.
Committed to standing with Border Patrol and ICE agents to secure the border and remove criminal illegal immigrants.
Says a one-size-fits-all federal approach does not work; supports empowering states and parent choice, including career and technical education.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy approach, addressing burdensome regulations and rejecting federal overreach while protecting the environment.
Fighting to lower barriers large financial institutions have built around essential services and to bring financial tools within reach of everyone.
"The United States is the greatest country the world has ever known."
"Our Nation was founded on Judeo-Christian values. We need God, and we trust in His plan."
"American-made energy powers more people, protects more people, and lifts more people out of poverty than government handouts."
"Agriculture is paramount to National Security."
"Our border must be secure."
Says the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms is fundamental to a free society, calling it "the freedom that secures the First Amendment rights."
Says growing federal intervention in education has come at the expense of state and local control and burdened teachers with paperwork.
Supports American liquefied natural gas exports, saying they help Texans and reduce allies' dependence on gas from hostile regimes like Russia and Iran.
"More government is not the answer. More spending is not the answer. More taxes are not the answer"; calls for cutting spending and limiting government.
Says the House has a duty to use its "power of the purse" to restrain and punish adversaries while supporting global allies.
Committed to bipartisan work to reduce deficits and long-term debt, and to helping every American who wants a job find one.

H0TX24209.name: Beth Van Duyne
H0TX24209.bio: U.S. Representative serving on the Ways and Means and Small Business Committees.

positions.stance: Working for limited-government policies, cutting federal regulations and a pro-growth tax code so families keep more of what they earn.
A strong supporter of school choice, believing parents, not the federal government, have the primary stake in their child's education.
Supports an all-of-the-above approach to expand domestic energy production, calling energy dominance essential for lowering costs and fighting inflation.
Opposes the Affordable Care Act and supports expanding insurance options to lower costs while protecting people with pre-existing conditions.

H2TX33040.name: Roger Williams
H2TX33040.bio: Chairman of the House Small Business Committee who has run a family-owned car dealership and cattle operation for over 50 years.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower taxes and cut burdensome regulations that hurt small businesses and stifle economic growth.
Says he has delivered more funding for warfighters through record defense spending and supports military families.
"I will always fight for the top-notch healthcare, compensation, and benefits" veterans deserve.
"America does not have a revenue problem - we have a spending problem"; says Washington must do more to live within its means.
Says people know how to spend their money better than government; supported the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and making tax relief permanent.
Calls China "our most aggressive adversary" and supports rebalancing American foreign policy to meet its threats.
Supports lowering taxes, reforming the legal system to limit undue business liability, and cutting burdensome regulations to help small businesses.
Supports an all-of-the-above domestic energy approach focused on clean energy technology, and opposes offshore drilling, especially off Florida.
Says immigrants are vital to South Florida and supports policies that secure the border while respecting that diversity and community.
Supports new trade partnerships to expand markets as long as agreements are free and fair, protecting American producers from unfair practices.
